features.t: Event buses (default + custom; create, describe, list, delete, tags)
Rules (create with event pattern, describe, list, delete, enable/disable, tags)
Rule Builder (visual canvas)
x: The visual Builder is a real editor over the rule's event pattern and targets: drawing a Triggering event wired to Target nodes is exactly what PutRule/PutTargets send. It has no sample-event library or schema-registry discovery; advanced pattern operators (prefix, anything-but, numeric, exists) go in the 'Other pattern fields' JSON or the pattern editor.

features.t: Targets (SQS, SNS, Lambda, Step Functions, Kinesis)
x: Only SQS, SNS, Lambda, Step Functions state machines and Kinesis data streams are actually invoked. Other target types (API destinations, ECS tasks, CodeBuild/CodePipeline, Batch, Systems Manager, ...) are accepted and stored by PutTargets like the real API, but PutEvents never delivers to them — there is no silent fake success, the delivery simply never happens.

features.t: PutEvents — pattern matching + fan-out to matching rules' targets
Archives (capture a bus's events matching a pattern)
x: An archive filters the bus's most recent 500 events (a bounded in-memory log), not a true unlimited-retention store, so RetentionDays can only be enforced within that window — it cannot bring back events the 500-event cap already dropped.

features.t: Replay — redeliver archived events to their original rule targets
x: Replay is synchronous (completes inside the StartReplay call, not asynchronously over minutes) and is bounded by the same 500-event archive window as eventbridge.archives.

features.t: Scheduler: schedules (one-time at(), rate(), cron()) and schedule groups
Scheduler: target delivery (SQS, SNS, Lambda, Step Functions, Kinesis) when a schedule's time arrives
x: Vyomi has no background timer. A schedule's firing is computed and delivered the next time any Scheduler API call is made after its due time (console navigation and the periodic list/describe calls it makes are usually enough) — it does not fire on the wall clock while nothing is polling.

features.t: CloudWatch metrics (Invocations, TriggeredRules, MatchedEvents, FailedInvocations; Scheduler attempts/errors)
Pipe metrics (Execution, ExecutionSucceeded, ExecutionFailed, Duration)
Pipes (create, describe, list, update, start/stop, delete) with SQS source -> target delivery
x: Only SQS queues are a delivering pipe source; Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, MSK, MQ sources are accepted and stored but never polled. Enrichment, source filter criteria and target input templates are stored and not applied - the raw message body is forwarded.

features.t: Connections (API key / basic / OAuth credentials; create, describe, list, update, deauthorize, delete)
API destinations (HTTP endpoint + connection + method; usable as a rule target)
x: CRUD is real on both substrates. Offline delivers a real HTTP request to InvocationEndpoint with the connection's API-key/basic auth; OAuth client-credentials token exchange is not performed and InvocationRateLimitPerSecond is stored but not throttled. On Nano the browser sandbox cannot make an arbitrary outbound request, so delivery counts as a FailedInvocation.

features.t: Global endpoints (failover routing config over two event buses)
x: Control plane is real (create, describe, list, update, delete with validation). Vyomi simulates one region so no Route 53 health check is evaluated and no failover/replication actually happens.

features.t: Sandbox: TestEventPattern (match an event against a pattern)
Event bus + archive encryption with a customer KMS key (events stored as real KMS ciphertext)
x: Encryption is applied to Vyomi's bounded per-bus event log through the real KMS core (Encrypt on PutEvents, Decrypt on archive read/replay); a disabled key blocks PutEvents and makes archived payloads unreadable. Key grants / key-policy checks for the events.amazonaws.com principal and the encryption-context binding are not modeled.

features.t: Event bus logs delivered to CloudWatch Logs (LogConfig Level/IncludeDetail)
x: Only the CloudWatch Logs destination is modeled (log group /aws/vendedlogs/events/event-bus/<bus>); S3 and Firehose log destinations and per-delivery-destination configuration are not. Records cover event receipt, rule-target invocation outcome, no-match and policy denial; they are emitted synchronously.

features.t: Event bus resource-based policy (PutPermission/RemovePermission) enforced on cross-account PutEvents
x: The caller's account comes from the x-amz-account-id request header (Vyomi has one real account; SigV4 is not verified). Evaluation covers Principal account/*, events:PutEvents/events:*/* Actions and explicit Deny; Condition blocks (aws:PrincipalOrgID, etc.) are stored but not evaluated. Policy is enforced for PutEvents only.

features.t: Attach an archive while creating an event bus
x: Console convenience: CreateEventBus has no archive parameter in the real API either; the console issues CreateArchive right after the bus is created, and so does Vyomi's.

features.t: EventBridge Schemas: registries, schemas and versions (REST CRUD, search)
x: The AWS-managed aws.events registry is not shipped; only registries and schemas you create or discover exist. Schema content is validated as JSON only (OpenApi3 / JSONSchemaDraft4 structure is not checked); code bindings and GetCodeBindingSource are not modeled.

features.t: Schema discovery: discoverers infer OpenAPI schemas from PutEvents on a bus
x: Inference is a structural JSON-type inference (string/number/boolean/object/array, nullable not modeled) producing OpenApi3; new versions are created when the shape changes. Cross-account and partner buses are not discovered.

features.t: Partner event sources: partner create/delete, customer activate, bus association, PutPartnerEvents delivery
x: Vyomi simulates one account, so the partner and the customer are the same account (the console's Vyomi SaaS partners play the partner role); there is no cross-account partner handshake and pending sources expire only when listed, with no background reaper. Real third-party SaaS partners (Datadog, Zendesk, ...) cannot push events into the simulator.
